text:
maria: getting a bunch of 429s from notify-proxy and the incident bot did not escalate to L2. customers are reporting delayed pages. anyone seeing this?
ops-bot: [ALERT] notify-proxy rate limiter tripped in prod-us-east-1 (service: notify-relay). auto-suppression engaged.
sam_k: looking. grabbing current metrics and PD logs.
rajiv: I can see a spike starting at 15:23 UTC, requests to /v1/notify jumped 4x from alert-router. vendor responses returned 429s, then our relay started returning 502s to callers.
lee_sre: confirmed, rate limiter on notify-relay hit burst threshold, relay entered backoff and incident-bot suppression rule kicked in.
support_jane: affected customers: Support queue shows ~34 incidents flagged as delayed paging, 2 escalations missed our 15-min SLO window so far. reaching out to impacted accounts now.
maria: okay let's do manual escalation for any open P1s. @lee_sre can you flip relay to fallback vendor and restart the process?
lee_sre: on it. plan: 1) bump rate-limit threshold temporarily, 2) enable fallback vendor routing, 3) rolling restart of notify-relay in us-east AZs.
rajiv: suggested command for restart (prod-us-east-1, canary then full):
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/notify-relay --context=prod-us-east-1-canary
sleep 60
kubectl -n infra rollout status deployment/notify-relay --context=prod-us-east-1-canary
# verify metrics, then run for the remaining AZs
```
lee_sre: canary restart done, saw error rate drop and 200s return to vendor. enabling fallback vendor now.
ops-bot: [INFO] fallback-vendor routing toggled ON by lee_sre at 15:42 UTC.
sam_k: metrics look better, request rate still high but success ratio up from 76% -> 98% after fallback.
support_jane: updated affected customers, sent initial incident notifications and ETA for remediation. no data exfiltration reported, purely delivery delay.
maria: good. can we also audit why incident-bot suppression logic suppressed escalations? that's big risk.
rajiv: quick cause: suppression rule checks notify-relay backoff state and suppresses pages if relay is in backoff to avoid spam. didn't account for vendor-fallback state where pages could still be delivered via SMS. rule false-positive.
lee_sre: action: open PR to change suppression predicate to allow L2 escalations if fallback vendors are enabled. also add metric that incident-bot watches: fallback_enabled==true => disable suppression.
maria: agree. create runbook step to manually toggle fallback in future incidents.
sam_k: I'll add a short term config change to increase burst threshold by 2x for 24h while we monitor.
support_jane: current customer impact: 34 delayed pages, 2 missed SLOs, ~3 customers reported operational impact (on-call didn't get page). logged and contacting CS leads now.
deploy-bot: [DEPLOY] Rolling restart completed for notify-relay in prod-us-east-1 (all AZs) by lee_sre at 15:47 UTC.
lee_sre: full restart complete. monitoring for 15m.
maria: thanks all. follow-up: assign postmortem owner and list action items (suppression rule change, runbook update, rate-limit tuning, alerting for fallback-state). I'll take postmortem owner.
sam_k: noted. I'll open the incident ticket and attach logs/metrics.
rajiv: also recommend adding synthetic paging tests that hit the full notify path including fallback.
support_jane: will send customer follow-ups once postmortem is ready.
maria: resolved for now, keeping thread open until postmortem published. :white_check_mark:
